stories.title: IBCC plans fully online attestation from Jan 1, ending office visits and courier submissions
summary: The Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC) will launch a fully online attestation service on Jan 1, 2027, allowing students to apply for attestation and download their attested documents without visiting an IBCC office or sending documents by courier.

Dr Mallah said the commission had developed the system on the directions of Federal Secretary for Education and Professional Training Nadeem Mahbub, after the IBCC Board of Governors took up the automation of the entire attestation process.
He said the commission expected the service to benefit an estimated 400,000 to 500,000 students by cutting travel and courier costs and saving them time spent visiting and waiting at IBCC offices.

stories.title: Search for Indonesia factory fire missing to resume on Monday, police remove 24 body bags
summary: Indonesian police removed 24 body bags from a factory destroyed by fire in Java on Sunday as firefighters battled remaining hotspots a day after the blaze tore through the building and a search for dozens of missing workers was suspended overnight.
Metro TV footage showed distraught family members weeping outside the factory as they waited for news of relatives feared to have been caught in the blaze.
Relatives of the missing victims flocked near the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones, footage aired by local broadcasters showed.

stories.title: Multiple Karachi routes briefly closed as political parties hold demonstration, rally
summary: The JUI-F staged its main demonstration at Guru Mandir, while the JSRC organised a rally from Sachal Goth to the press club via Sharea Faisal, some stretches of which had been shut for vehicles, the traffic police said.
The route from Guru Mandir towards Jamshed Road was reopened for vehicles at around 5pm after being closed to traffic shortly after 2pm.
Main Korangi Road from CSD towards Sharea Faisal was closed at around 11am due to “security” reasons and was reopened to traffic at 9:30pm.

stories.title: Pakistan Shaheens post 313 against India A in heated Rising Stars Asia Cup clash
summary: Pakistan Shaheens made 313 in 49.2 overs after winning a controversial toss and opting to bat against India A in their Asia Cup Rising Stars match here on Sunday, with half-centuries from Maaz Sadaqat, Hasan Nawaz and Farhan Yousaf underpinning their total.

Maaz Sadaqat plays a shot during the Asia Cup Rising Stars match against India A on Nov 22. — Photo courtesy ACC Maaz, registering his second consecutive half-century, made 59 off 63 balls, with six fours and a six, before being caught off Suryansh Shedge in the 20th over.

Hasan Nawaz plays a shot during Asia Cup Rising Stars match against India A on Nov 22. — Photo courtesy ACC Farhan Yousaf then struck 56 off 48 balls, hitting four fours and two sixes, while Mohammad Imran added a brisk 23 off 14 deliveries, including two sixes.

stories.title: 3 TTP-linked terrorists killed in village on outskirts of Peshawar: CTD
summary: PESHAWAR: Three terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire with Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and military personnel in the Passani village, located on Peshawar’s outskirts, late on Saturday night, the CTD said in a statement on Sunday.

The statement said the CTD received intelligence about the presence of a group of terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Khawarij on Passani Road — an area located 23 miles south of Peshawar, falling within the jurisdiction of Mattani police station.
However, upon seeing law enforcement and security personnel, the terrorists opened fire, to which the teams responded effectively in self-defence, the statement further said.

stories.title: Naqvi hits back at minister for repeated criticism: report
summary: Naqvi’s remarks have been reported a day after Inter-Provincial Coordination Minister Rana Sanaullah questioned the objectives of some of the businesspeople at that July forum.
Sanaullah further termed both Bilawal and Naqvi as “sons” of President Asif Ali Zardari, adding that they were “under his discipline”.

He himself calls him (Naqvi) his son; it is not that we are saying so.” Referring to a recent meeting between President Zardari and PM Shehbaz Sharif, during which Naqvi was also present, Sanaullah said a “ceasefire was decided” there.

stories.title: COP31 climate talks collapse as EU and others reject deal
summary: UN climate talks collapsed on Sunday as the European Union and others rejected a final draft deal put forward by COP31 presidents Turkiye and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.

Fossil fuels are driving the climate crisis. ” Australia’s COP31 President of Negotiations, Chris Bowen, called the outcome “very disappointing” and said disagreements over fuels and climate finance were the dealbreakers.
Developing countries had also criticised the deal for not providing sufficient new climate finance to help them adapt to a warming planet.

stories.title: Oman to supply petroleum products, $200m credit facility to PSO under new agreement
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Oman on Sunday signed an agreement under which the Gulf country’s state-owned OQ Trading would supply petroleum products, as well as a $200 million credit line, to the Pakistan State Oil (PSO).
Following the meeting, the two ministers witnessed the signing of a Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) for petroleum products between PSO and OQ Trading (OQT), Oman’s global commodity trading company.

According to the Petroleum Division, OQT’s LPG supplies to Pakistan are expected to exceed 120,000 metric tonnes by the end of 2026, reflecting the company’s continued commitment to meeting market demand and maintaining energy flows amid regional supply disruptions.

stories.title: Future wars
summary: THE four-day military confrontation between India and Pakistan last year and the US-Iran war this year have revealed how today’s wars have become far more complex than the conventional conflicts humanity has experienced over millennia.

Two distinguishing features of today’s warfare are advanced missiles and armed drones, which have transformed the nature of war by enabling high-precision, long-range, and rapid response capabilities.
The ability of a nation to acquire and em­­ploy modern technologies is thus critical to both wag­-ing future wars and surviving them.

stories.title: PTI MNAs demand to know whereabouts of party leaders detained in KP, seek their court production
summary: At the meeting, the lawmakers called for the immediate disclosure of the whereabouts of now non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, provincial president Junaid Akbar Khan and other detained party leaders and workers.

On governor’s rule and ongoing political situation The meeting also condemned reported raids on the homes of PTI workers and detentions under MPO following the imposition of governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11.
During the meeting, PTI leaders claimed that governor’s rule had further aggravated the province’s political, economic and administrative challenges.

stories.title: Veteran journalist Husain Naqi passes away in Lahore
summary: The premier remembered Naqi as a “principled journalist who fearlessly raised voice for freedom of expression, democratic values and human rights throughout his life”.
The president paid tribute to Naqi’s “services to journalism, freedom of expression and human rights”, the statement said.
After early schooling and college education in Lucknow, Naqi moved to Karachi in the 1950s, where he developed into a student leader.

stories.title: Pakistani among two injured in Iranian attacks, Bahrain says
summary: A Pakistani citizen was among two injured in last night’s Iranian attacks on Bahrain, authorities in the kingdom said on Sunday.
The attacks came as two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing its efforts to blockade the strategic shipping lane.

Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Tehran insists the programme is entirely civilian in nature. “I believe a solution can be found, but we have clear red lines: the material will not be taken out of the country,” Araghchi said.

stories.title: PPP, PML-N spat continues as Asif's jibe at Bilawal draws 'red line' warning
summary: In the latest from the ongoing wrangling between the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, the PPP, leaders from the latter have said Defence Minister Khawaja Asif’s remarks directed at Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari were “unacceptable” and crossed the party’s “red line”.

Did not know they would turn out to be masters of dishonesty and change colours so remarkably.” Reacting to his remarks, Rehman posted on X: “Unacceptable flow of comments from the federal defence minister about the PPP organisation and our leadership, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari.
In a statement posted on X, the PPP said Bilawal had directed party leaders to ignore the defence minister’s remarks and concentrate on issue-based politics.

stories.title: Naqvi warns fellow minister against repeated criticism
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday warned a fellow member of the cabinet against repeatedly criticising him, saying the minister would not be able to show his face if he responded to the remarks, Express News reported.
His remarks come amid criticism of Naqvi following his proposal for a new governance system and the creation of new provinces.

Calling Naqvi "a highly respected and credible member" of the cabinet, Asif said the interior minister had held some of the country's most influential positions over the past three and a half years and could have raised or pursued the issue of systemic reform during that period.

stories.title: Two successive drone attacks hit Bannu peace jirga, injuring 10
summary: At least 10 people, most of them young, were injured on Sunday morning when two successive quadcopter drone attacks targeted a tribal peace jirga in the Gul Badin Lundi Dak area of Bannu.
Local tribal elders and residents of the Sardi Khel tribe had gathered to discuss the security situation and draw up measures for restoring peace when the first drone struck.
In a separate incident, a drone attack was also reported on the residence of Malik Tawani, head of the Hathi Khel Peace Committee.

stories.title: Rs10b released to K-P under Rs160b uplift package
summary: For road infrastructure, Rs12.7 billion has been earmarked for 32 projects aimed at improving the road network in the designated districts.
An amount of Rs17.746 billion has been proposed for 11 special projects in these districts.
Another Rs12.64 billion will be spent on 61 projects related to health and education, according to the proposed allocations.

stories.title: At least 14 people missing after Russian drone hit building in Kyiv region, Zelenskiy says
summary: At least 14 people may still ​be trapped under the rubble ‌of a residential building that was struck by a ​Russian drone on ​Sunday morning in Ukraine's Kyiv ⁠region, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy ​said.
"Part of a five-story apartment ​building has collapsed following a Russian drone attack.
I thank ​our first responders for ​acting quickly: nine people have already ‌been ⁠evacuated, and the fire has been contained," Zelenskiy said on X.

stories.title: Trump says US to penalize firms building data centers abroad
summary: President Donald Trump said on Friday ​that the US would penalize American companies that build data ‌centers overseas, a move he said is intended to help the US artificial intelligence sector compete with its Chinese counterparts.
Several major American data center developers build and ​operate such facilities outside the US, including Equinix and Digital Realty.

The United States already bars direct sales of the most advanced AI chips to China, but Chinese ⁠companies have ​continued to access them by renting computing ​capacity at data centers in countries that can legally import the chips.

stories.title: Shaheens set a 314-run-target for India A in crucial Asia Cup match
summary: Hasan Nawaz struck a commanding 79 while Maaz Sadaqat and Farhan Yousaf also blasted fifties as Pakistan A were folded for 313 against India A in their Asia Cup Rising Stars Group B match in Doha on Sunday.
He struck five fours and four sixes in his 82-ball 79, sharing a 65-run partnership with captain Abdul Samad for the fourth wicket.
Farhan Yousaf smashed crucial 56 off 48 balls, hammering two sixes and four fours to boost the total.

stories.title: Bilawal warns US-Iran dialogue collapse could widen conflict, says Pakistan optimistic about settlement
summary: Pakistan People's Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari warned that the Iran-US conflict could spread beyond its current boundaries if the ongoing diplomatic process collapses, while expressing optimism that both sides would reach a settlement soon.
Bilawal said Pakistan had played a key role in securing the initial ceasefire and sustaining dialogue between the two sides, adding that Islamabad remained actively involved in the process.
According to Bilawal, Islamabad wanted to expand cooperation with Ankara beyond defence and strengthen economic ties to match the level of friendship between the two countries.

stories.title: COP31 climate talks see no consensus as EU, others reject deal
summary: The COP31 climate talks in Turkey neared a close on Sunday with no consensus on a final deal as countries argued over the pace of the clean-energy transition, the role of carbon capture, and financial support for developing nations.

You should not hurt people ​in the world who really expect something out of this by just being hung up on one word or phrase... there is no benefit for anyone in ‌a system where you go into negotiations with no result." "There will be no new text from now on.
We will not be forced to accept false solutions.

stories.title: Like SpaceX, Anthropic ran an unusual IPO process, chafing some bankers
summary: With SpaceX’s IPO in June, in which banks earned half a billion dollars in fees, bankers chafed over how tightly the Elon Musk-led company ‌controlled the months-long process and kept financial and other information private, making it hard for advisers to do their jobs.

Anthropic, for example, instructed some of its 22 IPO underwriters to limit the number of bankers working ​on the deal to four, asking the firms to make sure they were senior staff, several people familiar with the matter said.
Anthropic also used a product called NetRoadshow to share information, instead of regular PDFs, with most of the banks underwriting the deal.

stories.title: HEC to introduce MOFA attestation option on degree attestation portal
summary: In a major relief for thousands of students struggling with lengthy and cumbersome attestation procedures, the Higher Education Commission (HEC) decided to integrate the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) attestation option into its online degree attestation portal.
Under the proposed facility, students applying for degree attestation will also be asked whether they require attestation from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA).

The proposed feature will enable students to indicate their MOFA attestation requirements at the initial application stage, helping streamline and coordinate the degree attestation and verification process.

stories.title: Japan-Europe joint probe enters Mercury's orbit
summary: After an eight-year-long trek through outer space, the Japanese-European joint BepiColombo probe has entered Mercury's orbit, the European Space Agency (ESA) said on Sunday.
The European portion is set to study the planet's surface, skimming just 480 kilometres (300 miles) above Mercury.
The Japanese part, meanwhile, will follow an elliptical orbit that will take it as far as 11,000 kilometres from the planet in a bid to learn more about Mercury's magnetic field.

stories.title: Lahore once again ranks as world's most polluted major city as AQI crosses 500
summary: Lahore topped the list of the world’s most polluted major cities once again on Sunday morning with an hourly air quality index (AQI) reading of over 500, according to real-time air quality data.

Swiss air quality monitoring platform IQAir’s live global major city ranking placed Lahore first with 538 between 9am and 10am, classifying the quality as ‘hazardous’, indicating extremely polluted conditions and serious health risks for residents.
A day earlier, the Lahore Traffic Police claimed to have intensified enforcement operations against vehicles contributing to air pollution.

stories.title: Presidential ordinance withdraws most privileges of KP MPAs, including protection against preventive detention
summary: Two of the ordinances envisage setting up an executive committee with wide-ranging powers to oversee special initiatives, including developmental schemes, in the 12 designated districts and the rest of the province, respectively.
The committee will have powers to identify and recommend the executing agency for special initiatives in the designated and other districts, including military formations.

Both the ordinances provide for the establishment of an executive committee comprising a chairman, vice chairman and other such members as nominated by the prime minister, in case of designated district, and by the governor of the province, in case of the remaining districts.

stories.title: Broken record: UN entry, Mountbatten’s prejudice and the Grand Mufti’s letter

Washington’s man in Karachi Another major diplomatic development during this period was the appointment of America’s first ambassador to Pakistan.

stories.title: PML-N, PPP tug-of-war intensifies as Sherry warns Asif over fresh jibe at Bilawal
summary: On November 19, Asif shared two video clips of Bilawal, one from an earlier parliamentary speech and another from his recent address at the Karachi Press Club (KPC).
Over the past few days, Asif had repeatedly posted about Bilawal, sharing another clip of the PPP chairman speaking in an interview with a private news channel on November 20.
Responding to the PPP chairman's assertion that he was a stakeholder in the system, Asif said Bilawal was “not just a stakeholder, perhaps the biggest beneficiary”.

stories.title: Dar, Saudi FM discuss possible R4 meeting on regional developments
summary: The two leaders discussed cooperation at… pic.twitter.com/TVWiYHU9Xl — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) November 22, 2026 Renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have drawn repeated condemnation from Pakistan.

On November 20, the Foreign Office called a strike on a tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District a “grave violation” of Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, warning that attacks on civilian and economic infrastructure threatened regional peace and security.
Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government have since claimed hundreds of strikes on Houthi-held territory.

stories.title: South Korean education minister offers to resign amid AI-assisted cheating controversy
summary: South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin on Sunday offered to resign, taking responsibility for confusion caused by last-minute changes aimed at preventing AI-assisted cheating during the country's national college entrance exam, local media reported.
The Suneung is the Korean abbreviation for the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), the country's annual college entrance examination, which was held Thursday.

stories.title: Markets, schools in Rawalpindi to remain open during Punjab CM’s visit
summary: Arrangements are being made in Raja Bazaar, Commercial Market and along Murree Road for the chief minister’s visit.

The local administration has directed educational institutions to continue their routine activities during the visit of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, making it clear that no institution or market will be closed.

Meanwhile, Shahid Ghafoor Paracha, president of the Anjuman Tajraan Rawalpindi, said the chief minister would inaugurate the pedestrian streets in Raja Bazaar and Commercial Market and review development work in the garrison city.

stories.title: Israel, US agree to develop joint plans for possible escalation against Iran: report
summary: According to Channel 13, Israeli army assessments suggested that "the time has come for US President Donald Trump to decide on taking action in Iran." The report followed months of tensions after the US and Israel launched military attacks against Iran on February 28.

Trilateral meeting focuses on military readiness On Wednesday, Cooper met with Israeli army Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and Mossad chief Roman Gofman in Tel Aviv amid preparations for the possibility of renewed attacks on Iran.
Israeli media reported that Gofman met CIA Director John Ratcliffe to discuss Israeli intelligence assessments and the possibility of renewed military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Three police officials booked over forged performance evaluation reports in Rawalpindi
summary: Following an inquiry report, a case was registered at the Civil Lines police station against the three police personnel, including the in-charge of the CRC branch.

According to the inquiry report, several ACRs and PERs of JPO and SPO officers were being completed and cleared through the said email address and login, while OTP messages received on the email account were also allegedly being accessed by the computer operator.
According to the inquiry, the in-charge sent the letter without proper verification, while the concerned branch in Lahore informed the former SSP Investigation about the matter.

stories.title: Seven body bags recovered, 50 missing after Indonesian factory fire
summary: Indonesian police recovered seven body bags and rescuers were searching for about 50 workers who were missing on Sunday after a fire tore through a factory in western Java, as firefighters tackled hotspots over a day after the blaze broke out.

Authorities said the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable via visual inspection, prompting efforts to collect DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers.

Read: How haze from Indonesian fires impacts Southeast Asia To aid identification efforts, authorities are collecting DNA samples from the relatives of missing workers and gathering personal belongings from their homes or dormitories to help establish the victims' identities.

stories.title: Prisoner injured as woman opens fire in Mansehra courtroom
summary: Shoaib Fazal, 36, the prisoner, said in his complaint to the police that he was present in the court of the Additional Sessions Judge when Nosheen Bibi opened fire on him at around 11am, leaving him injured.
The woman not only committed contempt of court but also created an atmosphere of fear among the people by opening fire on me,” he added.
The Mansehra police had registered an FIR in September last year on the complaint of the woman, who had stated that Fazal, a friend of her husband, had kidnapped her 14-year-old daughter.

stories.title: Zardari-Shehbaz meeting to help ease tensions: Kundi
summary: SWABI: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Saturday that Thursday’s meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari in Islamabad would help ease tensions between the two ruling parties.
Governor inaugurates new building of Swabi hospital The governor said that the prime minister and the president agreed that all matters should be resolved through dialogue.
Mr Kundi said the first meeting of the Advisory Council held after the imposition of the governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa prioritised security, education and health sectors.

stories.title: Reflective vests made mandatory for KP police on VIP duty
summary: RAWALPINDI: To ensure the security and safety of police personnel deployed on VVIP/VIP movement duty, wearing high-visibility reflective vests has been made mandatory.

The SP Security said it had been observed that police officers and officials wore different types of jackets and caps during VVIP/VIP duties, making it difficult to determine whether they were private individuals or law enforcement personnel.

Reflective vests are intended to improve the safety of police personnel by making them easily identifiable and visible to drivers from a distance, particularly at night, when they may face various risks while performing their duties.

stories.title: Forensic evidence points to servant in Hina Javaid murder as probe clears husband
summary: Hina Javaid’s husband and his father have been cleared of any involvement in the murder by the police investigation, as no evidence linking them to the crime has been found.
Although Hina Javaid’s husband and her father-in-law were named in the initial FIR registered on murder charges, they were given a clean chit in the police investigation.

The Punjab government had constituted a three-member high-powered committee to review the investigation into the murder case, in which her husband and a domestic servant had been placed on judicial remand at Adiala Jail.

stories.title: Veteran journalist, human rights activist Hussain Naqi passes away
summary: Veteran journalist and human rights activist Hussain Naqi died in Lahore on Sunday, prompting tributes from President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
The HRCP said it deeply mourned the death of Naqi, whom it described as a veteran journalist, trade unionist and human rights defender.

It added that Naqi had served the commission in different capacities for three decades and remained an active member of its council at the time of his death. “One of the strongest voices for people’s rights and democracy in Pakistan has gone silent,” the HRCP said.
